 Judgment

This is a charge sheet filed by the PI of CCB (F& M), Bommanahalli Police Station, Bengaluru against the accused for the offences punishable U/Sec.51(1) (b), 63 of Copy Right Act & Sec.420 IPC.
02.

The brief facts of the prosecution case is that, on 11.12.2017 at about 4.40 pm., within the limits of Bommanahalli Police Station, at SS Fashions, 345/2, 6th Main, 5th Cross, Chamundeshwari Nagar, Devarachikkanahalli Road, Bengaluru, CW.1 got information that, the accused was selling the spurious/counterfeit garments i.e., pants of LOUIS PHILIPPE of CW.2 company without obtaining any permission from company authorities to the public and cheated to the companies and also C.C.No.27947/2018 public and thus the accused has committed the offences punishable U/Sec.51(1) (b), 63 of Copy Right Act & Sec.420 IPC.
03.

After filing of charge sheet, this court took cognizance for the offences punishable U/Sec.51(1)
(b), 63 of Copy Right Act & Sec.420 IPC and issued summons to the accused.
Accordingly the accused appeared before the court through his counsel and released on bail.

Later on, charge sheet copies and prosecution papers were furnished to the accused under Sec.207 of Cr.P.C.
04.
Heard both side on framing of charge, perused the prosecution papers.

As there are sufficient materials to frame the charge against the accused, the charges has been framed for the offence punishable U/Sec.51(1) (b), 63 of Copy Right Act & Sec.420 IPC and the same was read over to him,
but he denied the contents of charge and claimed for trial.
Hence, the case was posted for prosecution evidence.
05. In furtherance of the charges leveled against the accused, the following points are arisen for my consideration.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on 11.12.2017 at about 4.40 pm., within the limits of Bommanahalli Police Station, at summons Fashions, 345/2, 6th Main, 5th Cross, Chamundeshwari Nagar, Devarachikkanahalli Road, Bengaluru, CW.1 got information that,
the accused was selling the spurious/counterfeit garments i.e., pants of LOUIS PHILIPPE of CW.2 company without obtaining any permission from company authorities to the public and cheated to the company and also public and thus the accused has committed the offences punishable Nagaraj

2 U/Sec.51(1) (b), 63 of Copy Right Act & Sec.420 IPC?
02. What order or sentence?
06. To prove the case, the prosecution has examined the witnesses i.e., CW.7 as PW.1, CW.6 as PW.2 and CW.8 as PW.3.
PW.1 not tender himself for cross examination.

CW.1 to 4 are not examined before this court, CW.5 is given up and got marked the documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.5 and also marked material objects as MO.1 to 6.
07.
After completion of evidence of prosecution, the incriminating circumstances in the evidence of the prosecution is read over to the accused and statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C. recorded.
The accused has denied the incriminating circumstances as false and not chosen to lead his side defence evidence.
Heard the arguments.

My findings on the above said points are as follows:-
Point No.1 : In the negative. Point No.2: As per final order, for the following:
REASONS 09.
Point No.1:

To prove the case, the prosecution has examined CW.7 as PW.1, who being the Investigation Officer has deposed about receiving of complaint, registering crime and submitting of FIR and he handed over the case file to CW.8 for further investigation.
PW.1 has not tendered himself for cross examination inspite of sufficient opportunities given to him.
10. Further, CW.8 as PW.2, CW.6 as PW.3 they are official witnesses.
CW.3 & 4 accompanied with PW.2 & 3 to conduct raid.

The PW.2 & 3 deposed that, they went to spot i.e., SS Fashions, No.345/1,
6th Main, 5th Cross, Bengaluru and seized counterfeit/spurious 700 LP Company pants, 50 half stitched pants, 2100 LP Company buttons, 35 LP company tags, 50 LP company packing poly bags by conducting of Panchanama
and separated one LP company C.C.No.27947/2018 pant for the purpose of its genuineness examination.

Thereafter, they visited SHA Garments No.90/1, 2nd Floor,
Manjunatha Reddy Building, Hongasandra along with staff and panch witness as per the clue given by the accused.

sentences.text: Wherein, they found 25 stitching machines and 8 laborers stitching the cloths.

They did not find any LP Company products and conducted the spot panchanama at the spot further produced the PF before the court and deposed about releasing of accused on bail and obtaining statements of CW.3 to 6.

On 30.12.2017 he sent the seized LP Company Pant along with requisition to the authority of Anvesh IPR company for its genuineness report and he received the report on 21.03.2018 and submitted the charge sheet before the court.
In the said process CW.6/ PW.3 assisted PW.2 and typed the panchanama in the laptop as per the dictation of PW.2.
Thereby, they supported the case of prosecution.

sentences.text: It is pertinent to note here that, PW.2 deposed that, he has seized the material objects in the presence of panchas and conducted the panchanama at the spot.

But, the said panch witnesses i.e.,
CW.3 & 4 are not appeared before this court to say C.C.No.27947/2018 their versions.
Further, CW.1 being the complainant and CW.2 being the representative of Anvesh IPR Services also not appeared before this court to say their versions.
Hence, prosecution failed to prove the Ex.P.5 panchanama.

Further, it is significant to note here that, the said seized alleged counterfeit/ spurious LP COMPANY cloths, buttons, tags and packing poly bags will not come under the purview of section 13 of Copy Right Act.

Section 13(1) of Copy Right Act reads as under;
"Section 13. Works in which copyright subsists.

(1) Subject to the provisions of this section and the other provisions of this Act,
copyright shall subsist throughout India in the following classes of works, that is to say,--
(a) original literary, dramatic, musical and artistic works;
(b) cinematograph films; and (c) 1[sound recording]".

Such being so, this court has relied upon the order passed by Hon'ble High Court of Judicature, at Madras passed in Crl. OP.No.6357/2021 and Crl.M.P.No.4248 and 4249/2021, wherein para No.7,
it is held that;
" para No.7:- ..... it is clear that, unless the infringement relates to original literary,
dramatic, musical and artistic works, Cinematograph films and sound recordings, the provisions of the Act are not applicable.

entities.text: High Court of Judicature, at Madras
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In the instant case, there are no C.C.No.27947/2018 such allegations, hence, the offences punishable U/Sec. 63 of the Copy Right Act, 1957 is not made.
Such being so, for the reasons, provision and decision discussed supra, this court cannot come to conclusion that, the accused has committed the alleged offences.
Hence, the doubt arises in the mind of the Court regarding the case of the prosecution to bring home the guilt of the accused.

Thus,
there are no any incriminating materials to establish the alleged offence leveled against the accused.
Therefore, the prosecution has utterly failed to prove the alleged offences against the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.
Hence, I answered the Point No.1 in the negative.
12. Point No.2:-

In view of the findings recorded to the above points, this court proceed to pass the following:
ORDER

By exercising powers conferred U/sec. 248(1) of Cr.P.C., the accused is acquitted for the offences punishable U/Sec.51(1) (b), 63 of Copy Right Act & Sec.420 IPC The bail bond and surety bond of the accused shall continue in force for a period Nagaraj

4 of 6 months.
The accused is set at liberty.
The Mo 1 to 6 reported in PF No.87/2017 being pants, buttons, tags and bags are ordered to be destroyed as worthless after appeal period is over.

(Sri. Vinod Balnaik.)
